A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SMoPE study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the conference-format conversion and added material in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original continual-learning experiments on ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, and CUB-200, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline results, a 50-task ImageNet-R evaluation, and temporal activation and accuracy analyses.

M1.justification: The shared prompt, attention-score aggregation, sparse expert selection, adaptive noise, router and prototype losses, and additional training strategies are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same training algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate class-incremental learning on ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, and CUB-200. The added 50-task partition changes the experimental split within existing coverage, rather than introducing a new dataset, domain, or task requirement.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated ConvPrompt and CPrompt comparisons on all three datasets while retaining every previous comparator. The comparator sets in the existing self-supervised, computational-cost, and task-count comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 and Table 6 extend the ImageNet-R protocol from 5-, 10-, and 20-task partitions to include 50 tasks. Existing metrics, backbones, prompt configurations, preprocessing, and the 20% validation split are retained.

E4.justification: The task-count sensitivity study gains a longer sequence. New Appendix D.7 examines expert activation across successive tasks, and D.8 examines accuracy trajectories on CUB-200. The component ablations and previous prompt-length, noise, loss-weight, prototype, and convergence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run averages and the same plus/minus reporting convention for the main comparisons and component ablations. The additional table entries follow existing practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, run-count increase, or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds ConvPrompt and CPrompt scores, 50-task results, and temporal findings in Figures 10–11. The new 50-task SMoPE results are FAA 75.54 ± 0.49 and CAA 81.94 ± 0.93. Table 3 revises Deep L2P++'s reported parameter count from 1.33M to 4.78M without changing its Table 5 configuration. Previously reported matched accuracy results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the strong-identifiability definition, Voronoi loss, Theorems A.2–A.3, convergence rates, and proof arguments. Changes near the covering-number derivation concern notation and prose rather than mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient shared prompting, reduced interference, adaptive expert utilization, prototype-based retention, and competitive performance. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendices D.7–D.8 extend the mechanism discussion by interpreting progressive expert diversification as protecting earlier knowledge and attributing OVOR's declining accuracy trajectory to simultaneous prompt updates. The existing qualifications about interference over indefinitely long task sequences and evaluation limited to ViT remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a public-code availability statement and SMoPE repository address in the abstract, plus a reproducibility statement. Existing hardware, optimizer, augmentation, hyperparameter, and baseline-implementation disclosures are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, not whether the repository is operational.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Gao et al. (2024) and Roy et al. (2024), discussing prompt growth and external-language-model overhead in their approaches. V2 removes the citation to Le et al. (2025), On the Expressiveness of Visual Prompt Experts. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained. Local edits include proof prose, expanded related-work and baseline descriptions, new appendix subsections, a reproducibility statement, and Appendix E's editorial-use disclosure. Author notes and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The conference-template conversion changes typography, headers, text density, and figure/table placement throughout both main text and appendices. Existing graphics are resized and regrouped, Table 1 gains rows, Table 6 gains a 50-task column group, and Figures 10–11 are added. The original nine figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the existing evaluation with two relevant baselines, a longer task sequence, and temporal diagnostics, while adding code-access information. These provide useful incremental support and transparency without changing the core method, theory, or earlier accuracy findings. The denser layout makes some tables smaller, but the added evidence supports a limited net improvement.
